newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel doubts U.S. aid to be Clinton pressure tool.
newsitem.headline: Israel doubts U.S. aid to be Clinton pressure tool.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Wednesday he doubted re-elected President Bill Clinton would use U.S. aid to pressure Israel into making concessions on peace with Arabs.
"I don't believe pressure helps -- on the contrary," he told Channel One Television.
Israel receives more U.S. aid each year than any other country -- $1.8 billion for defence and $1.2 billion in economic aid -- and raises money abroad with the help of U.S. loan guarantees.
"When Israel is asked to take difficult decisions, to take risks, even on security, the last thing which must be done is to try to harm its defence capability," Meridor said.

"In the end the thing is, the aid is given in its entirety to defence purchasing and payment of debts for security. So it wouldn't be wise. Therefore I imagine they won't use aid for pressuring Israel."

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, after his election in May, told the U.S. Congress that Israel would over the next four years begin a long-term process of gradually reducing U.S. economic assistance.

But Meridor told the television: "In the coming year we have a difficult problem of balance of payments and I imagine also for the year after. We are not taking into consideration any lowering of the American aid."

Israel and the Palestinians resumed negotiations on Wednesday night on a long-delayed Israeli troop pullback from Hebron, the last of seven West Bank cities due to be given Palestinian self-rule under a 1995 peace deal.
Israel wants to boost security for the 400 Jews who live and study in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs.
